title: Matteo Berrettini Discusses Mental Struggles Ahead Of Paris Masters Match With Humbert

 Matteo Berrettini opened up about the mental challenges of dealing with repeated injuries as he prepares to face Ugo Humbert at the 2026 Paris Masters.
 by Anushka Raghav | Nov 04, 2026 | 2 minute read Matteo Berrettini reflects on the mental toll of his injury struggles ahead of his Paris Masters clash with Ugo Humbert. · Credits; Via ATP Tennis Matteo Berrettini began his 2026 Paris Masters campaign with a win over American Brandon Nakashima in the first round. The Italian will now face France’s Ugo Humbert in the round of 32 as he looks to continue his run in Paris. After the victory, Berrettini spoke about how years of injuries have changed the way he thinks about his body, handles pain and deals with his emotions. He admitted that he often overthinks small signs of discomfort but is learning to stay calm and accept what happens.
 Berrettini Learns to Handle Pain and Fear After Injuries
 Berrettini said that he now understands his body better than before. He knows when to push himself and when to take a break. However, he believes that people often forget about the mental challenges that come with the injuries.
 “Now, I know my body a little better and I know when I can push and when I can’t. But I think the mental side is largely underestimated,” he said.
 After dealing with severe injuries, even small pain can now make him worry that something serious might have happened. He explained that once he believed everything depended on his physical condition, but however he has now learned to stay calm and listen to his body.
 “When you get injured often, your brain automatically reacts to every pain and thinks something is wrong,” Berrettini explained. He added that tennis is a demanding sport, both physically and mentally. Players have to accept that sometimes these challenges and learn how to deal with them. Throughout his career, he struggled with injuries in his hand, abdomen, ankle and hip. After reaching the Wimbledon final in 2021 and rising to world No. 6, repeated injuries often stopped him from making further progress.
 Italian Admits He Often Overthinks
 Berrettini also admitted that his thoughts and emotions can sometimes make life harder.
“I’d say I’m someone who overthinks. I have a lot going on in my head and I also feel things very intensely. I like being that way, but sometimes it doesn’t help me with what I do,” he said.
 He believes players should trust themselves instead of worrying about every possible problem. “You shouldn’t overthink or let your emotions carry you away. You simply have to follow your instincts,” he added.
 He also explained that life on tour moves very quickly. “Our lives move very fast. I often say that one year for us is worth seven,” he said, referring to the constant travel and busy schedule.
 These experiences help him take a step back from a sport he loves but which can sometimes feel overwhelming. As he admitted, “Feeling things is positive, but sometimes I wish I could switch off my brain a little and enjoy moments without overanalyzing them.”
